'''Horst Sachs''' (27 March 1927 – 25 April 2016) was a German [[mathematician]], an expert in [[graph theory]], a recipient of the [[Euler Medal]] (2000).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tu-ilmenau.de/index.php?id=44015|title=Horst Sachs 1927 - 2016|work=tu-ilmenau.de|accessdate=4 May 2016|archive-date=25 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160625054605/https://www.tu-ilmenau.de/index.php?id=44015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He earned the degree of [[Doctor of Science]] (Dr. rer. nat.) from the [[Martin-Luther-Universität Halle-Wittenberg]] in 1958.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=60099}}.</ref> Following his retirement in 1992, he was [[professor emeritus]] at the Institute of Mathematics of the [[Technische Universität Ilmenau]].<ref>[http://www.tu-ilmenau.de/fakmn/Sachs-Horst.sachs.0.html Faculty profile at Ilmenau], retrieved 2010-08-07.</ref>

His encyclopedic book in [[spectral graph theory]], ''Spectra of Graphs. Theory and Applications'' (with Dragos Cvetković and Michael Doob) has several editions and was translated in several languages.<ref>[[VEB Deutscher Verlag der Wissenschaften]], Berlin, 1980. Academic Press, 1980. 2nd ed., [[VEB Deutscher Verlag der Wissenschaften]], 1982. 3rd revised and enlarged ed., Johann Ambrosius Barth, Heidelberg, 1995, {{ISBN|978-3-335-00407-3}}. Russian translation ''Spektry grafov. teoriia i primenenie'', Naukova dumka, Kiev, 1984.</ref><ref>Review by [[Lowell W. Beineke]] (1981), ''SIAM Review'' '''23''' (4): 546–548, {{doi|10.1137/1023115}}.</ref><ref>Review by Gordon J. Savage and S. Toida (1981), ''Journal of the Franklin Institute'' '''311''' (6): 403, {{doi|10.1016/0016-0032(81)90029-6}}.</ref><ref>Review by [[Bojan Mohar]] (1995), {{Zbl|0824.05046}}.</ref><ref>Review by Wessel (1996), [[Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics]] '''76''' (10): 144, {{doi|10.1002/zamm.19960760305}}.</ref><ref>Review by P. Rowlinson (1996), ''Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society (Series 2)'' '''39''': 188–189, {{doi|10.1017/S0013091500022902}}.</ref>

Two theorems in graph theory bear his name. One of them relates the coefficients of the [[characteristic polynomial]] of a graph to certain structural features of the graph. Another one is a simple relation between the characteristic polynomials of a graph and its [[line graph]]. [[Sachs subgraph]]s are also named after Sachs.
